findings.summary: INVALID_CREDENTIALS is used as an error outcome but is not a member of AuthErrorCode.
findings.detail: AuthErrorCode enumerates six values and does not include INVALID_CREDENTIALS. The code is nonetheless returned by Login R2, by LoginRequestToSession validation, and asserted in workflows.md, capabilities/login.md, STORIES.md US-02, TEST-SPEC.md and UI-SPEC.md. Either the enumeration is incomplete or the code is out of vocabulary.
findings.consequence: AuthErrorCode cannot be treated as the closed error vocabulary.

findings.summary: Principal omits the identifier and credentialHash fields its own operations require.
findings.detail: domain.md#principal declares id, subjectType, status, roleKeys, directPermissions. Login R1 and R2 resolve a principal by identifier and verify a credential; SeedSystemBootstrap C2 constructs a principal with identifier and credentialHash; LoginRequestToSession maps identifier to principalId by principal-resolution. Neither field is declared on the entity.
findings.consequence: The entity definition is incomplete against its declared behavior.

findings.summary: Canonical-key invariant I1 forbids the wildcards the domain requires.
findings.detail: I1 is ^[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-zA-Z0-9*]+$ so * is admissible only in the action segment. decisions.en.md confirms wildcard support for service.*.* and *.*.*; PermissionResolutionPolicy evaluates a globalWildcard tier; the extracted admin role grants player-management.*.*, player-makeup.*.* and financial-settlement.*.*. RoleDefinition invariants simultaneously require every role permission key to match I1. Separately, the PermissionKey value object constrains scope to kebab-case and action to camelCase, which admits no wildcard at all.
findings.consequence: The canonical-key rule is self-contradicting; confirmed decisions and seeded example grants violate the invariant they are declared to satisfy.

findings.summary: Deny-overrides is undecidable on the declared authorization input.
findings.detail: AuthorizeRequest decides over authContext.permissions typed as a deduplicated string[], itself sourced from Session.effectivePermissions, also string[]. A flat string list cannot carry PermissionGrant.effect, so no DENY is representable at decision time, yet R3 states exists denyMatch => decision = DENY and the policy ranks deny above every allow tier. The documents never say whether DENY grants are applied during resolution and dropped, or are expected to survive into the decision.
findings.consequence: The deny-overrides commitment has no defined carrier.

findings.summary: Two lifecycle triggers are not in the domain-event catalog.
findings.detail: states.md drives Session ACTIVE to EXPIRED on SessionExpired and AccessToken ACTIVE to EXPIRED on TokenExpired. events.md defines exactly five domain events and neither is among them, so two of the declared transitions are triggered by events with no definition, payload, or consumer.

findings.summary: Project domain scope and DomainSpec domain scope disagree.
findings.detail: DEF-AUTH-UM-001 defines the project as packaging auth domain, session transport, user/resource authorization and provider link management; DEF-AUTH-UM-003 defines provider connection as a domain term; DEC-AUTH-TRANSPORT-001 commits to hybrid cookie plus bearer transport. The DomainSpec docs contain no ProviderConnection concept, no cookie-session concept and no ownership-based authorization concept, while README.md and docs/ADOPTION.md push OAuth providers and cookie transport out to consumers.
findings.consequence: The ledger's domain and the SPEC's domain are not the same domain.

findings.summary: Example roles are asserted as acceptance requirements.
findings.detail: README.md and domain.md#roledefinition state that roles are consumer-provided and the extracted Poker Team roles are examples only, not exported as package defaults. SeedSystemBootstrap R4 and C3 require grants for all predefined roles, and US-11 asserts as an acceptance check that all four role definitions (admin, manager, coach, player) have grants, itemizing example permissions per role.
findings.consequence: The story treats documented examples as the domain.

findings.summary: AuthAPI is registered as a domain concept but declared out of scope.
findings.detail: README.md#boundaries states the package does not own HTTP routes, yet interfaces.md defines AuthAPI with five REST routes and SPEC.md registers auth-access-control.AuthAPI in the Concept Registry with three exposes edges into Login, AuthenticateRequest and AuthorizeRequest. A concept the package disclaims is a first-class node in its concept graph.
findings.consequence: Boundary ambiguity between domain concept and consumer-contract example.
findings.note: auth-access-control.AuthAPI is deliberately NOT a node in this graph: it is system-branch and the package disclaims it. Recorded here as an unresolved boundary question.

findings.summary: The login risk policy is unnamed and unregistered.
findings.detail: Login R3 depends on riskPolicy(context) with three deterministic deny conditions and three context defaults. Unlike PermissionResolutionPolicy it has no concept ID, no entry in the Concept Registry and no policy section in workflows.md.
findings.consequence: Load-bearing domain policy the ontology cannot address by an owned name.

findings.summary: No precedence between Principal.directPermissions and principal-scoped grants.
findings.detail: PermissionGrant.granteeType admits principal, and Principal also carries directPermissions. Login C2 feeds both into resolvePermissions. No rule defines their relative precedence, nor whether a principal-scoped DENY grant overrides a listed direct permission.
findings.consequence: Permission resolution is underspecified. Related to CON-04 but independently unresolved.

findings.summary: No business outcomes or value measures are defined.
findings.detail: The outcome and value-measure roles have zero instances. The domain defines behaviors, rules and guarantees but no target outcome that would let anyone judge whether the auth domain is achieving its purpose rather than merely executing its rules.
findings.consequence: The domain cannot be evaluated against intent, only against conformance.

findings.summary: Service and automation principals have no modeled path.
findings.detail: subjectType admits user, service and automation. Every rule, story, policy and default is written for the human-user path: identifier plus password, user-agent presence as a risk signal, IP reputation. A service principal that legitimately has no user agent is denied by the risk policy as written. No story, rule or exception covers non-human principals.
findings.consequence: Two of three admitted principal kinds are unreachable under the stated policy.

findings.detail: R2 requires minTtl <= ttlSeconds <= maxTtl, but neither bound is defined anywhere in the domain documents and no decision fixes them, while the session TTL beside it is a fixed domain constant of 8 hours.
findings.consequence: Two different TTL governance styles, one unresolved.

intentional_asymmetries.summary: Authentication collapses session state into AUTH_REQUIRED while introspection expands it into five reasons.
intentional_asymmetries.rationale: decisions.en.md confirms that session expiry rejects requests as AUTH_REQUIRED.
